\chapter{Chapter07 — PCPP Three Query}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.PCPPThreeQuery}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Clause excluding an assignment]
\lean{FABL.excludingClause}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.excludingClause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.SignCube}
For a sign assignment $x\in\{−1,1\}^r$, form a conjunction of one literal for each
coordinate $i$, requiring that coordinate to have sign $-x_i$. Thus the term is false on
$x$ and has no repeated coordinate indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of the excluding clause]
\lean{FABL.excludingClause_width}
\label{FABL.excludingClause_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.SignCube, FABL.excludingClause}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $r$ and every sign assignment on $r$ coordinates, the
width of the clause constructed from that assignment is $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of an excluding clause]
\lean{FABL.excludingClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.excludingClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.SignCube, FABL.excludingClause}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $a$ and $x$ be sign assignments on the $r$
coordinates. The clause constructed to exclude $a$ evaluates to $−1$ at $x$ if and only
if $x\ne a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Truth-table CNF formula]
\lean{FABL.truthTableCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.truthTableCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.SignCube, FABL.excludingClause}
Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on sign vectors of length $r$. Form a CNF formula
with one clause for each sign vector $x$ on which $f(x)=1$, where that clause excludes
$x$ by using, at each coordinate, the sign opposite to $x$; the formula has no clauses
for inputs on which $f$ is not $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the truth-table CNF]
\lean{FABL.truthTableCNF_size_le}
\label{FABL.truthTableCNF_size_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.truthTableCNF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $r\ge 0$ and let $f:\{\pm1\}^r\to\{\pm1\}$. The CNF formed with one clause for each
assignment on which $f$ equals $+1$ has at most $2^r$ clauses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width of a truth-table clause]
\lean{FABL.truthTableCNF_clause_width}
\label{FABL.truthTableCNF_clause_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.excludingClause_width, FABL.truthTableCNF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r\ge 0$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^r\to\{\pm1\}$, and form the truth-table CNF with one
clause excluding each assignment $a$ for which $f(a)=+1$. Every clause that occurs in
this formula has width exactly $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the truth-table CNF]
\lean{FABL.truthTableCNF_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.truthTableCNF_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.eval, FABL.CNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.SignCube, FABL.excludingClause, FABL.excludingClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.truthTableCNF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r\ge 0$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^r\to\{\pm1\}$, and form the CNF having, for each
assignment $a$ with $f(a)=+1$, a clause that is false exactly at $a$. For every
$x\in\{\pm1\}^r$, this CNF evaluates to $-1$ if and only if $f(x)=-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width of the truth-table CNF]
\lean{FABL.truthTableCNF_width_le}
\label{FABL.truthTableCNF_width_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff, FABL.truthTableCNF, FABL.truthTableCNF_clause_width}
\difficulty{3}
Let $r\ge 0$ and let $f:\{\pm1\}^r\to\{\pm1\}$. The maximum width of the clauses in the
truth-table CNF formed from the assignments on which $f$ equals $+1$ is at most $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Local transcript]
\lean{FABL.localTranscript}
\label{FABL.localTranscript}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive tester for Boolean-valued functions on a disjoint union of an
input domain of size $n$ and a proof domain of size $\text{proofLength}$, making $r$
possible queries. For a seed of $V$ and a Boolean answer at each of the $r$ positions,
define the local transcript to record that answer wherever the tester queries an
address, and to record no answer where it makes no query.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local acceptance sign function]
\lean{FABL.localAcceptancePredicate}
\label{FABL.localAcceptancePredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive tester with Boolean answers and $r$ query positions, and fix a
seed. For each assignment of signs to those positions, convert the signs to Boolean
values and evaluate the tester's acceptance predicate on the resulting local transcript.
Define the sign-valued function to be $-1$ when the predicate accepts and $+1$
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of local acceptance]
\lean{FABL.localAcceptancePredicate_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.localAcceptancePredicate_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SignCube, FABL.localAcceptancePredicate, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let a Boolean proof-checking system make $r$ nonadaptive queries, fix a random seed, and
let $a\in\{-1,1\}^r$ be a sign assignment to the query positions. Convert each sign in
$a$ to its corresponding bit, and form the local transcript by placing that bit at each
queried position and leaving unqueried positions blank. The local acceptance function
takes the value $-1$ at $a$ if and only if the verifier accepts this transcript.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Seedwise three-CNF reduction]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.eval, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SignCube, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
Let $V$ be a PCPP system with Boolean alphabet, input length $n$, proof length $L$, and
$r$ queries, and let $K$ be a positive integer. A seedwise three-CNF reduction assigns
to every verifier seed a CNF formula on $r+K$ variables with exactly $K$ clauses, each
having between one and three literals. For every seed and every queried-bit assignment,
the verifier accepts exactly when there exists an assignment to the $K$ auxiliary sign
variables that makes the formula evaluate to $-1$ on the extended assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local prefix embedding]
\lean{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
\label{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
\leanok
For natural numbers $a$ and $K$ with $a\le K$, define the embedding from positions in a
list of length $r+a$ into positions in a list of length $r+K$ that preserves the first
$r$ positions and sends each of the remaining $a$ positions to the corresponding
position among the final $K$ positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding of the initial coordinates]
\lean{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding_castAdd}
\label{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding_castAdd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a\le K$. Under the natural inclusion of the
first $r$ coordinates into a tuple of length $r+a$, the embedding into a tuple of length
$r+K$ sends each such coordinate to the same coordinate: for every $i<r$, its image is
the coordinate $i$ in the longer tuple.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding of the appended coordinates]
\lean{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding_natAdd}
\label{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding_natAdd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a\le K$. The embedding of tuples of length
$r+a$ into tuples of length $r+K$ sends each appended coordinate $i<a$ to the appended
coordinate with index $i$ after the first $r$ coordinates, viewed in the larger block of
length $K$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Extension of a local literal]
\lean{FABL.liftLocalLiteral}
\label{FABL.liftLocalLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
Let $r,a,K$ be natural numbers with $a\le K$, and let a literal on $r+a$ coordinates
have coordinate $i$ and required sign $s$. Its lift to $r+K$ coordinates has coordinate
given by the local prefix embedding of $i$ and required sign $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lifting a local clause]
\lean{FABL.liftLocalClause}
\label{FABL.liftLocalClause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.liftLocalLiteral, FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a\le K$, and let a clause be a conjunction of
literals on $r+a$ coordinates, with no coordinate repeated. Its lift is the clause on
$r+K$ coordinates obtained by applying the local-prefix embedding to each literal,
preserving the literals’ required signs.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width preserved by lifting]
\lean{FABL.liftLocalClause_width}
\label{FABL.liftLocalClause_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.liftLocalClause}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r,a,K$ be natural numbers with $a\le K$, and let a clause on $r+a$ sign coordinates
have pairwise distinct literal indices. Its width, defined as the number of literals, is
unchanged when the clause is lifted to $r+K$ coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restricting a local assignment]
\lean{FABL.restrictLocalAssignment}
\label{FABL.restrictLocalAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.localPrefixEmbedding}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a\le K$, and let an assignment give a sign in
$\{\pm1\}$ to each of $r+K$ coordinates. Its restriction to the local prefix of size
$r+a$ assigns to each coordinate the sign at its image under the local-prefix embedding.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a lifted clause]
\lean{FABL.liftLocalClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.liftLocalClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.SignCube, FABL.liftLocalClause, FABL.liftLocalLiteral, FABL.restrictLocalAssignment}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r,a,K$ be natural numbers with $a\le K$. Take a clause on $r+a$ sign coordinates
whose literals use pairwise distinct coordinates, and an assignment of signs to $r+K$
coordinates. The lifted clause evaluates to $-1$ on that assignment if and only if the
original clause evaluates to $-1$ on the assignment restricted along the coordinate
embedding from $r+a$ coordinates into $r+K$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Filler auxiliary index]
\lean{FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex}
\label{FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex}
\leanok
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a+3\le K$. For each $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, the
filler auxiliary index is the coordinate in the $r+K$ coordinate set obtained by adding
$r$ to $a+j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of auxiliary indices]
\lean{FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex_injective}
\label{FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex}
\difficulty{3}
Let $a,K,r$ be natural numbers with $a+3\le K$. The map sending $j\in\{0,1,2\}$ to the
coordinate in the block of $K$ indices, offset by $r$, whose within-block index is
$a+j$, is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three-literal filler clause]
\lean{FABL.fillerClause}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002}
\label{FABL.fillerClause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.ofThree, FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex, FABL.fillerAuxiliaryIndex_injective}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a+3\le K$. The filler term on $r+K$
coordinates consists of three literals, each requiring sign $-1$, on three distinct
designated auxiliary coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of the filler clause]
\lean{FABL.fillerClause_width}
\label{FABL.fillerClause_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.fillerClause}
\difficulty{1}
Let $a,K,r$ be natural numbers with $a+3\le K$. The filler clause formed from the three
auxiliary coordinates has width $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padding a CNF to a fixed clause count]
\lean{FABL.padThreeCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002}
\label{FABL.padThreeCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.fillerClause, FABL.liftLocalClause}
Let $r,a,K$ be natural numbers, and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $r+a$ coordinates
with at most $K$ clauses. If $a+3\le K$, there is a constructed CNF formula on $r+K$
coordinates with exactly $K$ clauses: positions below the number of clauses of $\psi$
use its corresponding lifted clauses, and all remaining positions use filler clauses.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the padded formula]
\lean{FABL.padThreeCNF_size}
\label{FABL.padThreeCNF_size}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.padThreeCNF}
\difficulty{1}
Let a conjunctive normal form on $r+a$ sign variables have at most $K$ clauses, and
suppose $a+3\le K$. The padded formula has exactly $K$ clauses.
\end{theorem}

Let a conjunctive normal form on $r+a$ sign variables have every clause of width $3$,
and suppose its number of clauses is at most $K$ and $a+3\le K$. Every clause in the
padded formula on $r+K$ sign variables has width $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padding an auxiliary assignment]
\lean{FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment}
\label{FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a\le K$, and let an assignment give a sign in
$\{\pm1\}$ to each of $a$ auxiliary coordinates. Its padding to $K$ coordinates agrees
with that assignment on the first $a$ coordinates and is constantly $-1$ on the
remaining coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of existing auxiliary coordinates]
\lean{FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment_castLE}
\label{FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment_castLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $a$ and $K$ be natural numbers with $a\le K$, and let $u:\{0,1\}^a\to\{-1,1\}$ be an
auxiliary sign assignment. After extending $u$ to $K$ coordinates by retaining its first
$a$ coordinates and filling the rest with $-1$, its value at coordinate $i$ is $u(i)$
for every $i\in\{0,1\}^a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Values at the filler coordinates]
\lean{FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment_filler}
\label{FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment_filler}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $a$ and $K$ be natural numbers with $a\le K$ and $a+3\le K$, and let $u$ be a sign
assignment on $a$ coordinates. Extending it to $K$ coordinates by filling new
coordinates with $-1$ gives value $-1$ at each of the three coordinates $a,a+1,a+2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Taking an auxiliary prefix]
\lean{FABL.prefixAuxiliaryAssignment}
\label{FABL.prefixAuxiliaryAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube}
Let $r,a,K$ be nonnegative integers with $a\le K$, and let an assignment give a sign in
$\{\pm1\}$ to each of $K$ auxiliary coordinates. Its prefix of length $a$ assigns to
each of the first $a$ coordinates the same sign as the original assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction after padding auxiliary signs]
\lean{FABL.restrictLocalAssignment_extend_pad}
\label{FABL.restrictLocalAssignment_extend_pad}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment, FABL.restrictLocalAssignment}
\difficulty{4}
Let $a\leq K$, let $x$ be a sign assignment on $r$ original coordinates, and let $y$ be
a sign assignment on $a$ auxiliary coordinates. Extend $x$ by the auxiliary assignment
obtained by appending $K-a$ copies of $−1$, then restrict to the first $r+a$
coordinates. The result is exactly the extension of $x$ by $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction of an extended sign assignment]
\lean{FABL.restrictLocalAssignment_extend_prefix}
\label{FABL.restrictLocalAssignment_extend_prefix}

Let $a\leq K$, let $x$ be a sign assignment on $r$ original coordinates, and let $y$ be
a sign assignment on $K$ auxiliary coordinates. Restrict the extension of $x$ by $y$ to
its first $r+a$ coordinates. This equals the extension of $x$ by the restriction of $y$
to its first $a$ coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of satisfiability under padding]
\lean{FABL.padThreeCNF_complete}

assignment to $K$ coordinates with filler values $-1$ makes the padded formula evaluate

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three-query budget]
\lean{FABL.threeQueryBudget}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.threeQueryBudget}
\leanok
For a nonnegative integer $r$, define the budget to be $r2^r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Seed acceptance CNF]
\lean{FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF}
\leanok

Let $V$ be a nonadaptive tester with Boolean answers and $r$ query positions, and fix a
seed of $V$. The seed acceptance CNF is the truth-table CNF of the local acceptance
predicate on sign assignments to those positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Seedwise width-three CNF]
\lean{FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}

\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF, FABL.widthThreeTseitin}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive tester with Boolean answers and $r$ query positions, fix a
seed, and let $m$ be the number of clauses in its seed acceptance CNF. The seedwise
width-three CNF is the width-three Tseitin construction on that CNF, with $r+(r-3)m$
coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Seed acceptance formula size bound]
\lean{FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF_size_le}

its verifier. The size of the CNF formula encoding acceptance for seed $s$ is at most
$2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Seed acceptance formula width bound]
\lean{FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF_width_le}

Let $V$ be a Boolean PCPP system with $r$ verifier queries, and let $s$ be any seed of
its verifier. The width of the CNF formula encoding acceptance for seed $s$ is at most
$r$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF_size_le}

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Auxiliary-variable budget bound]
\lean{FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF_auxiliary_add_three_le}

\begin{theorem}[Clause width in the three-width conversion]

Let $V$ be a Boolean PCPP system with $r$ verifier queries, and let $s$ be any seed of

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Seedwise three-CNF reduction]
\lean{FABL.canonicalSeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.canonicalSeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.eval, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SignCube, FABL.localAcceptancePredicate, FABL.localAcceptancePredicate_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.padAuxiliaryAssignment, FABL.padThreeCNF, FABL.padThreeCNF_clause_width_eq_three, FABL.padThreeCNF_complete, FABL.padThreeCNF_size, FABL.padThreeCNF_sound, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.restrictCNFAssignment, FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF, FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF, FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF_auxiliary_add_three_le, FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF_clause_width_eq_three, FABL.seedWidthThreeCNF_size_le, FABL.threeQueryBudget, FABL.truthTableCNF_eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.widthThreeTseitin_complete, FABL.widthThreeTseitin_sound}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive tester with Boolean answers, input length $n$, proof length
$\ell$, and $r$ query positions, where $3\le r$, and put $K=r2^r$. For each seed, the
construction gives a three-CNF formula on $r+K$ sign coordinates with exactly $K$
clauses; each clause contains between one and three literals, with distinct coordinates.
For every seed and every string of $r$ Boolean answers, the tester accepts the
corresponding local transcript if and only if the answers, encoded as signs, can be
extended by an assignment to the $K$ auxiliary coordinates so that the formula is
satisfied.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Truth-table size and query budget]
\lean{FABL.truthTableCNF_size_le_threeQueryBudget}

Let $r$ be a positive natural number and let $f:\{\pm1\}^r\to\{\pm1\}$. The truth-table
CNF formed from the assignments on which $f$ equals $+1$ has at most $r2^r$ clauses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Single-literal filler clause]
\lean{FABL.smallQueryFillerClause}

\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.ofOne}
Let $r,K\in\mathbb N$ with $K>0$. The filler term on $r+K$ coordinates consists of one
literal, requiring sign $-1$, on the first auxiliary coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of the filler clause]
\lean{FABL.smallQueryFillerClause_width}
\label{FABL.smallQueryFillerClause_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.smallQueryFillerClause}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r$ be a natural number and let $K$ be a positive natural number. The filler clause
on $r+K$ coordinates has width exactly $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Small-query seed CNF construction]
\lean{FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}

\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.liftLocalClause, FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF, FABL.smallQueryFillerClause, FABL.threeQueryBudget}
Let $V$ be a PCPP system with Boolean alphabet, input length $n$, proof length
$	ext{proofLength}$, and $r>0$ query positions, and let $s$ be a seed of its verifier.
The construction produces a CNF formula on $r+r2^r$ variables with exactly $r2^r$
clauses: in order, these are the lifted clauses of the seed acceptance CNF, followed by
copies of its first clause if it is nonempty; if it is empty, the clauses are the
prescribed filler clauses.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the padded seed formula]
\lean{FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF_size}
\label{FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF_size}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF, FABL.threeQueryBudget}
\difficulty{1}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive verifier with Boolean input alphabet, input length $n$, proof
length $p$, and $r>0$ query positions, and let $s$ be one of its seeds. The associated
padded seed CNF has exactly $r2^r$ clauses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a lifted clause]
\lean{FABL.liftOriginalClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}

\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.SignCube, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.extendCNFAssignment_castAdd, FABL.liftLocalClause, FABL.liftLocalClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.localPrefixEmbedding, FABL.localPrefixEmbedding_castAdd, FABL.restrictLocalAssignment}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r$ and $K$ be natural numbers, let $C$ be a conjunction of literals on $r$ sign
coordinates whose literal indices are pairwise distinct, and let $x$ and $y$ be sign
assignments on $r$ coordinates and $K$ auxiliary coordinates, respectively. Extend $x$
by $y$ to an assignment on $r+K$ coordinates, and lift $C$ to those coordinates by
placing its indices in the first $r$ positions. The lifted clause evaluates to $-1$ on
the extended assignment if and only if $C$ evaluates to $-1$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonempty clauses in the seed formula]

\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive verifier with Boolean input alphabet, input length $n$, proof
length $p$, and $r>0$ query positions, and let $s$ be one of its seeds. Every clause

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width bound for seed formula clauses]
\lean{FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF_clause_width_le_three}

\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt_mem, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.liftLocalClause_width, FABL.localAcceptancePredicate, FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF, FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF, FABL.threeQueryBudget, FABL.truthTableCNF_clause_width}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive verifier with Boolean input alphabet, input length $n$, proof
length $p$, and $r$ query positions, where $0<r<3$, and let $s$ be one of its seeds.
Every clause occurring in the associated padded seed CNF on $r+r2^r$ coordinates has
width at most $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Small-query seedwise three-CNF reduction]
\lean{FABL.smallQuerySeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.smallQuerySeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt_mem, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.CNFFormula.eval, FABL.CNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFTerm.ofOne, FABL.Literal, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SignCube, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.extendCNFAssignment_natAdd, FABL.liftLocalClause, FABL.liftOriginalClause_eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.localAcceptancePredicate, FABL.localAcceptancePredicate_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.seedAcceptanceCNF, FABL.smallQueryFillerClause, FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF, FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF_clause_nonempty, FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF_clause_width_le_three, FABL.smallQuerySeedCNF_size, FABL.threeQueryBudget, FABL.truthTableCNF_eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.truthTableCNF_size_le_threeQueryBudget}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system making $r$ possible queries, where $0<r<3$. Then
there is a seedwise reduction with $K=r2^r$ auxiliary sign variables and clauses. For
every seed it gives a CNF formula on the $r+K$ coordinates, with exactly $K$ nonempty
clauses, each of width at most three; for every assignment to the $r$ queried bits, the
verifier accepts its local transcript if and only if the formula is satisfiable by some
assignment to the $K$ auxiliary variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Seedwise three-CNF reduction]
\lean{FABL.positiveSeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.positiveSeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.canonicalSeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.smallQuerySeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.threeQueryBudget}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system making $r$ possible queries, with $0<r$. Then
there is a seedwise reduction with $K=r2^r$ auxiliary sign variables and clauses. For
every seed it gives a CNF formula on the $r+K$ coordinates, with exactly $K$ nonempty
clauses, each of width at most three; for every assignment to the $r$ queried bits, the
verifier accepts its local transcript if and only if the formula is satisfiable by some
assignment to the $K$ auxiliary variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Verifier description size]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system with a finite seed space. Its description size
is the number of possible seeds, namely the cardinality of the verifier's seed set.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Three-query proof length]
\lean{FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system with proof length $L$, and let $K$ be a natural
number. The associated three-query proof length is $L+K$ times the number of possible
verifier seeds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Indexing the verifier’s seeds]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.seedIndexEquiv}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.seedIndexEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize}
Let $V$ be a nonadaptive tester for Boolean-valued functions on inputs of length $n$,
with proof length $\ell$ and $r$ query positions. The seed space of its verifier is
equivalent to the set of integers from $0$ through one less than the size of that finite
seed space.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Default outer query address]
\lean{FABL.outerQueryAddress}
\label{FABL.outerQueryAddress}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem}
Let $n,\ell,r$ be nonnegative integers with $n>0$, and let $V$ be a PCPP system with
Boolean alphabet, input length $n$, proof length $\ell$, and $r$ query positions. For a
seed and a query position, its outer query address is the verifier’s specified address
when one is present, and otherwise is the first input coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lifting outer query addresses]
\lean{FABL.liftOuterAddress}
\label{FABL.liftOuterAddress}
\leanok
Let $n,\ell,K,s$ be nonnegative integers. The address map from the disjoint union of the
$n$ input coordinates and the $\ell$ proof coordinates to the disjoint union of the same
input coordinates and $\ell+Ks$ proof coordinates leaves every input address unchanged
and sends each proof address to the corresponding coordinate in the initial segment of
the enlarged proof space.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clause at a seed and index]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system making $r$ possible queries, let $K$ be a
natural number, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ have exactly $K$ clauses
for each seed. For a seed $s$ and an index $q\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$, the clause at $(s,q)$
is the $q$th clause of the CNF formula assigned to $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership of an indexed clause]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_mem}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_mem}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let a seedwise three-CNF reduction have a verifier with a finite seed space, and let a
seed and an index among its clauses be given. The clause selected by that index belongs
to the reduction's formula for that seed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonempty indexed clause]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_nonempty'}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_nonempty'}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_mem}
\difficulty{1}
Let a seedwise three-CNF reduction have a verifier with a finite seed space, and let a
seed and an index among its clauses be given. The selected clause contains at least one
literal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width bound for an indexed clause]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_width_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_width_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_mem}
\difficulty{1}
Let a seedwise three-CNF reduction have a verifier with a finite seed space, and let a
seed and an index among its clauses be given. The selected clause contains at most three
literals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padded literal at a clause position]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.literal}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.literal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.Literal, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_nonempty'}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system making $r$ possible queries, and let a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ have $K$ clauses for each seed. For a seed $s$, clause index
$q\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$, and position $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, the literal at position $j$ is the
literal of that clause whose list index is the remainder of $j$ upon division by the
clause width. Thus positions are taken cyclically when the clause has fewer than three
literals.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Literal occurrences in a clause]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.mem_clause_iff_exists_literal}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.mem_clause_iff_exists_literal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.Literal, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_nonempty', FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause_width_le, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.literal}
\difficulty{4}
Let a seedwise three-CNF reduction have a positive number $K$ of clauses, each nonempty
and of width at most three, with its stated completeness and soundness properties. For
any seed, clause index $q\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$, and literal $\ell$ over the $r+K$
variables, $\ell$ occurs in clause $q$ if and only if it is one of the three literals
obtained by taking the clause’s literal at position $j$ modulo its width, for some
$j\in\{0,1,2\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Composition query address]
\lean{FABL.compositionAddress}
\label{FABL.compositionAddress}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize, FABL.PCPPSystem.seedIndexEquiv, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.liftOuterAddress, FABL.outerQueryAddress, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions, and let $K$ be a positive integer. Given a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ with $K$ clauses, a seed of $V$ and a coordinate among the
$r+K$ local variables determine an address in the disjoint union of the $n$ input
positions and the $m+K|S|$ composed-proof positions, where $S$ is the finite seed set of
the verifier. For a coordinate among the first $r$ positions, this address is the outer
verifier’s query address (using input position $0$ when that query is absent), with
proof addresses shifted into the original proof block; for a coordinate among the final
$K$ positions, it is the auxiliary position indexed by that coordinate and the seed’s
index in $S$, after the original proof block.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Address of a composed literal query]
\lean{FABL.compositionLiteralAddress}
\label{FABL.compositionLiteralAddress}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.literal, FABL.compositionAddress, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions, and let $K$ be a positive integer. Given a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ with $K$ clauses, a verifier seed, a clause index among the
$K$ clauses, and one of three query positions determine the composed address of the
corresponding literal’s variable, in the disjoint union of the $n$ input positions and
the $m+K|S|$ composed-proof positions, where $S$ is the verifier’s finite seed set.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform clause distribution]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clauseDistribution}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clauseDistribution}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system making $r$ possible queries, and let a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ have $K>0$ clauses for each seed. Its clause distribution is
the uniform probability distribution on the $K$ clause indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Composed three-query verifier]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clauseDistribution, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.literal, FABL.compositionLiteralAddress, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $V$ be a Boolean-valued PCPP system with input length $n>0$, proof length $L$, and
$r$ possible queries. Given a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ with $K$ clauses per
seed, there is a nonadaptive Boolean tester making three queries on an input of length
$n$ and a proof of length $L+K$ times the number of possible verifier seeds. Its
randomness consists of a verifier seed and a uniformly chosen clause index. It queries
the three addresses corresponding to the clause's three padded literals, and accepts
exactly when at least one returned Boolean answer, interpreted as a sign, equals that
literal's required sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Composition into a three-query system]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQuerySystem}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQuerySystem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $n>0$, and let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions. Given a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ with
parameter $K$, the composed system has input length $n$, proof length $m+K s$ where $s$
is the number of seeds of $V$'s verifier, and exactly three query positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Seed of the composed verifier]
\lean{FABL.composedVerifierSeed}
\label{FABL.composedVerifierSeed}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions, and let $K$ be a positive integer. Given a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ with $K$ clauses, a seed of the original verifier and a
clause index among the $K$ clauses form a seed of the composed three-query verifier.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Distribution of composed verifier seeds]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier_distribution}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier_distribution}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clauseDistribution, FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier, FABL.composedVerifierSeed}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $\ell$, and query count $r$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ use
parameter $K$. The seed distribution of the composed verifier is the distribution
obtained by first sampling a seed from $V$'s verifier distribution and then sampling a
clause index uniformly from the reduction's $K$ clauses for that seed; the resulting
seed is the pair consisting of the sampled verifier seed and clause index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Composed local assignment]
\lean{FABL.compositionLocalAssignment}
\label{FABL.compositionLocalAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SignCube, FABL.compositionAddress, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions, and let $K$ be a natural number. Given a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ with $K$ clauses, a Boolean word on the disjoint union of
the $n$ input positions and the $m+K|S|$ composed-proof positions, and a seed of the
original verifier, define a sign assignment on the $r+K$ local variables by reading the
word at each coordinate’s composed address and converting that Boolean value to its sign
in $\{ -1,1\}$; here $S$ is the verifier’s finite seed set.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Composed verifier and clause evaluation]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier_accepts_iff}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier_accepts_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.literal, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.mem_clause_iff_exists_literal, FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier, FABL.compositionLiteralAddress, FABL.compositionLocalAssignment, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $\ell$, and query count $r$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ use
parameter $K$. For any Boolean word on the input and extended-proof addresses, and any
seed $(s,q)$ of the composed verifier, that verifier accepts the word at the seed if and
only if the clause indexed by $q$ for $s$ evaluates to $-1$ on the sign assignment
induced by the word at the corresponding composition addresses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Outer verifier local bits]
\lean{FABL.outerLocalBits}
\label{FABL.outerLocalBits}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.outerQueryAddress}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions, let $w$ be a Boolean input word of length $n$, and
let $p$ be a Boolean proof word of length $m$. For each verifier seed, the outer local
bit at each of the $r$ query positions is the value of the combined input-and-proof word
at the verifier’s query address, using input position $0$ when the query is absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Transcript from outer query bits]
\lean{FABL.localTranscript_outerLocalBits}
\label{FABL.localTranscript_outerLocalBits}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.outerLocalBits, FABL.outerQueryAddress}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be positive, and let a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$,
proof length $\ell$, and $r$ query positions be given. For every Boolean input word,
proof word, and verifier seed, the local transcript formed from the outer query bits
equals the verifier’s transcript obtained by querying the combined input and proof word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Local auxiliary witness]
\lean{FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness}
\label{FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SignCube, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.outerLocalBits}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $m$, and $r$ query positions, and let $K$ be a natural number. Given a seedwise
three-CNF reduction for $V$ with $K$ clauses, a Boolean input word of length $n$, a
Boolean proof word of length $m$, and a verifier seed, define a sign assignment on the
$K$ auxiliary variables as follows: if the verifier accepts the local transcript
obtained from the input and proof at that seed, choose an auxiliary assignment
witnessing satisfiability of the seed’s formula; otherwise assign the sign $-1$ to every
auxiliary variable.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfaction by the local auxiliary witness]
\lean{FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness_satisfies}
\label{FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness_satisfies}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.eval, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness, FABL.localTranscript, FABL.outerLocalBits, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be positive, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction associate a CNF formula with
each seed and satisfy the stated completeness and soundness properties. For any Boolean
input word of length $n$, proof word, and seed, if the verifier accepts the local
transcript obtained from the input and proof, then the formula associated with that seed
is satisfied by the assignment formed from the encoded local query bits followed by the
auxiliary assignment selected by the reduction’s local witness construction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Composed proof construction]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQueryProof}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQueryProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.seedIndexEquiv, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $V$ be a Boolean PCPP system with input length $n$,
proof length $m$, and $r$ query positions, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for
$V$ have parameter $K$. The map sends an input $w\in\{0,1\}^n$ and proof $p\in\{0,1\}^m$
to a Boolean string of length $m+K s$, where $s$ is the number of seeds of $V$: its
first $m$ entries are the entries of $p$, and each remaining entry encodes the
corresponding auxiliary sign assigned to a seed and query position.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Original proof coordinates in the composed proof]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQueryProof_castAdd}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQueryProof_castAdd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.composeThreeQueryProof}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $\ell$, and query count $r$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ use
$K$ auxiliary coordinates per seed. For every input word $w$, original proof $p$, and
index $i<\ell$, the composed proof agrees with $p$ at the corresponding original-proof
coordinate: its value at position $i$ in the initial block of length $\ell$ is $p(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Auxiliary proof coordinates in the composed proof]
\lean{FABL.composeThreeQueryProof_natAdd}
\label{FABL.composeThreeQueryProof_natAdd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.seedIndexEquiv, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.composeThreeQueryProof, FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $\ell$, and query count $r$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ use
$K$ auxiliary coordinates per seed. For every input word $w$, original proof $p$, seed
$s$ of $V$'s verifier, and auxiliary coordinate $q<K$, the composed proof at the
coordinate indexed by $(q,s)$ in its added block equals the Boolean encoding of the
$q$th coordinate of the local auxiliary witness chosen for $w$, $p$, and $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of the outer word under address lifting]
\lean{FABL.inputProofWord_composeThreeQueryProof_liftOuterAddress}
\label{FABL.inputProofWord_composeThreeQueryProof_liftOuterAddress}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.composeThreeQueryProof, FABL.composeThreeQueryProof_castAdd, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.liftOuterAddress}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a system with Boolean input of length $n$, proof length $\ell$,
and a finite random seed space, and let $K\in\mathbb N$. Suppose a reduction for $V$
supplies a three-CNF formula for each seed that is complete and sound for the verifier's
local acceptance predicate. For every input word
$w\colon\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\mathrm{Bool}$, proof word
$p\colon\mathrm{Fin}(\ell)\to\mathrm{Bool}$, and address in the disjoint union of input
and proof addresses, the word formed using the composed proof, evaluated at the lifted
address, equals the word formed using $w$ and $p$ at the original address.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Composed assignment identity]
\lean{FABL.compositionLocalAssignment_composeThreeQueryProof}
\label{FABL.compositionLocalAssignment_composeThreeQueryProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.composeThreeQueryProof, FABL.compositionAddress, FABL.compositionLocalAssignment, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.inputProofWord_composeThreeQueryProof_liftOuterAddress, FABL.localAuxiliaryWitness, FABL.outerLocalBits, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$, the original proof length $\ell$, and the query count $r$ be natural numbers,
and let $V$ be a Boolean PCPP system with these parameters. Let $K$ be a natural number
and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ with parameter $K$ be given; assume
$n>0$. For every input word $w\in\{0,1\}^n$, every proof word of length $\ell$, and
every verifier seed, the sign assignment obtained by evaluating the composed
input-and-proof word at the reduction's local addresses equals the extension of the
encoded outer local bits by the reduction's local auxiliary witness.
\end{theorem}

Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $\ell$, and query count $r$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ use
parameter $K$. If an input word $w$ and proof $p$ make $V$ accept with probability $1$,
then the composed three-query system accepts $w$ with the composed proof with
probability $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restriction to the original proof]
\lean{FABL.restrictOuterProof}
\label{FABL.restrictOuterProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $V$ be a Boolean PCPP system with proof length $m$ and verifier seed space of size
$s$, and let $K$ be a natural number. A Boolean proof word of length $m+Ks$ restricts to
a word of length $m$ by taking its first $m$ bits.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Extraction of local auxiliary bits]
\lean{FABL.extractLocalAuxiliaries}
\label{FABL.extractLocalAuxiliaries}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.seedIndexEquiv, FABL.SignCube, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with proof length $m$, a finite verifier seed
set $S$, and any number $r$ of query positions; let $K$ be a natural number. From a
Boolean proof word of length $m+K|S|$ and a verifier seed, define a sign assignment on
the $K$ auxiliary variables by reading, for each auxiliary position, the proof bit
indexed by that position together with the seed’s index in $S$, after the first $m$
proof bits, and converting the bit to its sign in $\{ -1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction of the extended proof at lifted addresses]
\lean{FABL.inputProofWord_restrictOuterProof_liftOuterAddress}
\label{FABL.inputProofWord_restrictOuterProof_liftOuterAddress}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.descriptionSize, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.liftOuterAddress, FABL.restrictOuterProof, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a system with Boolean input length $n$, proof length $\ell$, and a finite
random seed space, and let $K\in\mathbb N$. For every input word
$w\colon\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\mathrm{Bool}$, extended proof word
$q\colon\mathrm{Fin}(\ell+K|S|)\to\mathrm{Bool}$, and address in the disjoint union of
input and proof addresses, evaluating the word formed from $w$ and $q$ at the lifted
address gives the same value as evaluating the word formed from $w$ and the restriction
of $q$ to its first $\ell$ positions at the original address; here $|S|$ is the number
of seeds of $V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Local assignment from an extended proof]
\lean{FABL.compositionLocalAssignment_eq_extracted}
\label{FABL.compositionLocalAssignment_eq_extracted}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.compositionAddress, FABL.compositionLocalAssignment, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.extractLocalAuxiliaries, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.inputProofWord_restrictOuterProof_liftOuterAddress, FABL.outerLocalBits, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.restrictOuterProof, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$, the original proof length $\ell$, and the query count $r$ be natural numbers,
and let $V$ be a Boolean PCPP system with these parameters. Let $K$ be a natural number
and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction for $V$ with parameter $K$ be given; assume
$n>0$. For every input word $w\in\{0,1\}^n$, every extended proof of length
$\ell+K|\mathrm{Seed}(V)|$, and every verifier seed, the sign assignment obtained by
evaluating the concatenated input and extended proof at the reduction's local addresses
equals the extension of the encoded outer local bits, read from the first $\ell$ proof
positions, by the auxiliary signs extracted from the extended proof for that seed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A rejecting clause in the composed verifier]
\lean{FABL.exists_rejecting_composed_clause}
\label{FABL.exists_rejecting_composed_clause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.eval, FABL.CNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.clause, FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier, FABL.composeThreeQueryVerifier_accepts_iff, FABL.compositionLocalAssignment_eq_extracted, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.extractLocalAuxiliaries, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.localTranscript_outerLocalBits, FABL.outerLocalBits, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.restrictOuterProof, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n>0$, let a finite-randomness nonadaptive verifier have $r$ query positions and
proof length $\ell$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction have $K>0$ clauses per seed,
be complete, and be sound. For any input
$w:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, extended proof of length
$\ell+K$ times the number of seeds, and seed at which the original verifier rejects
using the restriction of that proof to its first $\ell$ proof bits, some clause index
$q\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$ makes the composed three-query verifier reject on the same input
and the full extended proof.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tester rejection indicator]
\lean{FABL.testerRejectionIndicator}
\label{FABL.testerRejectionIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester with domain $D$, alphabet $A$, and a finite query
budget, let $w:D\to A$ be a word, and let $s$ be a seed of $T$. The rejection indicator
is $0$ if $T$ accepts the transcript of querying $w$ with seed $s$, and $1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Rejection probability as an expectation]
\lean{FABL.rejectionProbability_eq_indicatorExpectation}
\label{FABL.rejectionProbability_eq_indicatorExpectation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one, FABL.testerRejectionIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let a nonadaptive tester have a finite seed space with probability law, query locations,
and a deterministic acceptance rule. For any function supplied to the tester, its
rejection probability equals the expectation over the seed of the indicator that the
tester rejects.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription_rejectionRate}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
Let $n\ge1$, let $V$ be a finite-seed nonadaptive verifier with Boolean input and proof,
input length $n$, proof length $\ell$, and $r$ query positions, and let $K>0$. Suppose a
reduction assigns to each verifier seed a CNF formula on $r+K$ sign variables with
exactly $K$ nonempty clauses of width at most three; for every transcript, the formula
is satisfiable by an auxiliary sign assignment exactly when the verifier accepts that
transcript. Let $w$ be a Boolean input word, let $p$ be a Boolean proof word of length
$\ell+K|\mathrm{Seed}(V)|$, and suppose the verifier rejects the word formed from $w$
and the first $\ell$ proof bits at some seed. Then, fixing that seed and choosing one of
its $K$ clauses uniformly, the expected rejection indicator of the composed three-query
verifier is at least $1/K$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription_rejectionRate}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b004}
Let $n>0$, let $V$ be a Boolean proof-checking system with input length $n$, proof
length $\ell$, and $r$ queries, and let a seedwise reduction with $K>0$ clauses
associate to each verifier seed a CNF formula of width at most three, satisfying
completeness and soundness for the verifier’s local acceptance predicate. For every
Boolean input word $w$ and every proof for the composed system, the rejection
probability of $V$ on $w$ and the restriction of that proof to its original proof
coordinates, divided by $K$, is at most the rejection probability of the composed
three-query system on $w$ and the given proof.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of property testing]
\lean{FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.isPCPP}

  {context}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001,

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b004}
\proofstep
  {FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription_rejectionRate}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b004}
Let $n$ be positive, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction be given for a Boolean PCPP
verifier. If the verifier is a probabilistically checkable proof system for a property
$P$ of Boolean words of length $n$ at rate $r_0>0$—meaning every word in $P$ has a proof
accepted with probability one, and every word at relative Hamming distance greater than
$␀$epsilon from every word in $P$ is rejected with probability greater than
$r_0␀$epsilon for all $0\leq\epsilon\leq1$ and every proof—then the composed three-query
verifier is a PCPP for $P$ at rate $r_0/K$, where $K$ is the reduction's positive clause
count.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three-query PCPP description]
\lean{FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPDescription, FABL.SeedwiseThreeCNFReduction.isPCPP, FABL.composeThreeQuerySystem, FABL.positiveSeedwiseThreeCNFReduction, FABL.threeQueryBudget, FABL.threeQueryProofLength}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of length $n$,
and let a PCPP description for $P$ have positive query count $r$. The construction
produces a PCPP description for $P$ with query count $3$, proof length given by the
three-query proof-length construction applied to the original verifier and the budget
associated with $r$, and rejection rate equal to the original rejection rate divided by
that budget.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
Let $n\ge 1$, let $P$ be a property of Boolean words of length $n$, and let a PCPP
description for $P$ have proof length $L$, positive query count $r$, and a finite
verifier seed set of size $S$. The proof length of the associated three-query PCPP
description is $L+r2^rS$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
Let $n\ge 1$, let $P$ be a property of Boolean words of length $n$, and let a PCPP
description for $P$ have positive query count. The associated three-query PCPP
description has query count $3$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,

  {FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription_queryCount}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
Let $n\ge 1$, let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of length $n$, and let a
probabilistically checkable proof description for $P$ have query count $r>0$ and
rejection rate $\rho$. The rejection rate of its three-query description is
$\rho/(r2^r)$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n,r$ be natural numbers with $n>0$, let $V$ be a probabilistically checkable proof
system whose verifier makes $r>0$ nonadaptive queries, and let $s$ be a seed of its
finite randomness space. For every $q<r2^r$, the list of literals at the three positions
of the clause indexed by $q$ in the canonical seedwise three-CNF reduction has length
exactly $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Reduction to three-query PCPPs]
\lean{FABL.semanticPCPPReductionToThreeQueries}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
\label{FABL.semanticPCPPReductionToThreeQueries}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.SemanticPCPPReduction, FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription}
Suppose that for every positive input length and every Boolean circuit on that input
length, a PCPP description is given for the property accepted by the circuit, and every
such description has a positive query count. Applying the three-query transformation to
each description defines a new reduction assigning a three-query PCPP description for
the same circuit-accepted property.
\end{definition}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b003}
Let a semantic PCPP reduction assign a PCPP description to every Boolean circuit on each
nonempty finite Boolean input cube, and suppose every verifier so obtained has a
positive query count. For any such cube and circuit, the proof length of the resulting
three-query description equals the original proof length plus the original query count
multiplied by $2$ to the power of that query count and by the cardinality of the
verifier's seed space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Output-sensitive three-query adapter]
\lean{FABL.ThreeQueryOutputSensitiveAdapter}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004}
\label{FABL.ThreeQueryOutputSensitiveAdapter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuitEncoding, FABL.OutputSensitivePCPPReduction, FABL.SemanticPCPPReduction, FABL.threeQueryPCPPDescription}
Let a Boolean circuit encoding and a semantic PCPP reduction be given, and suppose every
circuit's PCPP description has a positive query count. An output-sensitive adapter
consists of an output-sensitive PCPP reduction for that encoding whose semantic output,
on every Boolean circuit of positive input length, is exactly the three-query PCPP
description obtained by transforming the given reduction's output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial-time map from the adapter]
\lean{FABL.ThreeQueryOutputSensitiveAdapter.toPolytimeMap}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004}
\label{FABL.ThreeQueryOutputSensitiveAdapter.toPolytimeMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuitEncoding, FABL.OutputSensitivePCPPReduction.toPolytimeMap, FABL.PolytimeMap, FABL.ProofLengthPolynomiallyBounded, FABL.SemanticPCPPReduction, FABL.ThreeQueryOutputSensitiveAdapter}
Given a three-query output-sensitive adapter and a polynomial that bounds the proof
length of its semantic PCPP outputs in the size of each packed circuit, the adapter
determines a polynomial-time map from binary strings to binary strings.
\end{definition}
